conflict_topics: Shared pan left unwashed / dishwashing responsibility
dialogue_quality_notes: Dialogue is concise and realistic for flatmate negotiation — direct requests, short proposals, quick acceptance.
Some duplicated lines (Agent C's repeated phrasing) appear in the transcript, creating mild repetition.
Participants offered concrete proposals (times, fan/door rule, washing rule) rather than vague assurances.
evaluation.final_reason: The group reached concrete, accepted arrangements: scheduling was accommodated when Agent A offered to be done by 8:30 and Agent D accepted ('Okay. I can be done by 8:30. Would that work?' / 'Yeah, 8:30 is fine. Thanks.'). The smell concern was addressed when Agent B asked to keep the kitchen door closed and use the fan and Agent A agreed ('Can we please keep the kitchen door closed and use the fan when cooking?' / 'Okay. We can do that.'). The leftover pan was resolved when Agent A volunteered to wash it immediately and urged adherence to the new rule, and Agent C accepted ('I'll wash it now, and we all just stick to the new rule from tonight.' / 'Okay. That works. Thanks.').
position_change_notes: Agent A offered a concrete scheduling adjustment (will be done by 8:30) — moved from implicit late cooking to an earlier finish.
Agent D initially complained about access but explicitly accepted A's offered time ('8:30 is fine').
Agent B proposed a smell-control rule; Agent A accepted it (no further dispute).
Agent A volunteered to resolve the immediate dish issue (washing the pan), closing the remaining practical gap; Agent C accepted.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D: '...I get home from work and can't cook my own dinner.' Agent A: 'What time do you need to cook?' — D raises an incompatible practical need (evening stove access) but no agreement yet.
Agent D: 'I usually get home around 8.' Agent A: 'Okay. I can be done by 8:30. Would that work?' — A offers an accommodation on the scheduling conflict, but D has not yet accepted within this round.

Agent B: '...It's the smell. Can we please keep the kitchen door closed and use the fan when cooking?' Agent A: 'Okay. We can do that.' — The smell issue is explicitly raised and A agrees, but the earlier scheduling/stove-access issue remains unsettled.
Agent C: 'Okay, but we still have last night's pan in the sink.' — A new practical conflict (dirty shared pan) is introduced; previous scheduling and smell issues remain outstanding.

Agent D: 'Yeah, 8:30 is fine. Thanks.' (accepts the scheduling accommodation). Agent A: '...maybe we can just agree that whoever uses it, washes it straight after?' — Scheduling resolved; the washing rule is proposed but not yet fully assigned for the existing pan.

Agent C: 'Yeah, that's a good rule. So who's washing this one from last night?' — The new rule is endorsed (agreement on future conduct) but responsibility for the existing dirty pan is still unresolved.

Agent A: 'I don't know who left it. I'll wash it now, and we all just stick to the new rule from tonight.' Agent C: 'Okay. That works. Thanks.' — The outstanding practical issue (who cleans the pan) is concretely resolved by A volunteering to wash it and others accepting the house rule.
Agent C repeats acceptance/thanks ('Okay. That works. Thanks.') — no new substantive disagreement and previous issues remain settled.

substantive_insights: There were multiple overlapping, but separable issues: stove scheduling, smell mitigation, and dishwashing responsibility.
Simple, specific rules (close door/use fan; wash pans immediately) plus one-off cleanup (A washing last night's pan) resolved the practical frictions.
Resolutions combined clarification/house rules (fan/door), compromise on timing (A adjusting to D's schedule), and a concession (A washing the pan).
